_readme.what: Greenland d18O, a temperature proxy, at 20-year resolution from 60,000 BP to present. This is the film's SECOND environmental channel.
_readme.whyItExists: Sea level is slow and drives coastlines. Temperature is fast and drives sky, ice and mood. They are different physics and the film needs both. The 8.2 ka event is 160 years long and barely moves sea level at all - at the sea-level curve's 1,000-year sampling it does not exist. Here it is eight data points. Meltwater Pulse 1A is seventeen.
_readme.law01: A pure function of t, exactly like sea level. Neither channel reads the other; both read t. Adding this makes the architecture more correct without making it more complex.
_readme.units: yrBP = calendar years before present (1950), converted from the source's b2k by subtracting 50. d18O = permille, a temperature proxy where more negative means colder. errYr = maximum counting error in years at that depth, which Rasmussen et al. treat as 2 sigma.
_readme.notTemperature: d18O is a PROXY, not degrees. Do not put a temperature in Celsius on screen from this file. Normalise it and drive colour, haze and the drone with it.
_readme.coverage: 60 ka to present only. Beats 05 to 14 are covered. Beats 01 to 04 - including Toba at 74 ka - are NOT, and fall back to sea level alone. Extending to 123 ka needs the full NGRIP record; extending to 300 ka needs an ocean-core proxy instead, since no ice core reaches that far in Greenland.

source.cite: NGRIP members / Rasmussen, S. O. et al. GICC05 chronology, NGRIP d18O resampled to 20-year resolution, 0-60 ka b2k. Released 10 September 2007.
source.chronologyCite: Rasmussen, S. O. et al. (2014). A stratigraphic framework for abrupt climatic changes during the Last Glacial period based on three synchronized Greenland ice-core records. Quaternary Science Reviews 106, 14-28.
source.note: Same GICC05 chronology already cited in timeline.json for the Younger Dryas and the Holocene GSSP, so the film's climate events and its climate channel now share one time scale.

beatEvents.note: 160 years long. Invisible in the sea-level curve. Eight points here.
